record_verbatim.evidence: TOOLING. lldb is confirmed broken on this host, independently of this test: 'lldb --batch -o run -o "bt all" ./test_dp83869.out' dies at '(lldb) target create' with 'PLEASE submit a bug report', and the identical failure occurs on a two-line hello.c compiled in /tmp, so it is unrelated to this binary. ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/ does not exist and the emitted diagnostics.log is zero bytes, so no crash report is recoverable. gdb is not installed; the predecessor's bin/gdb shim has a Python 3 syntax error at line 64. AddressSanitizer was re-tried and does hang, at the LINK step, because the shipped ':tools: :test_linker:' appends -flto and LTO plus ASAN deadlocks this toolchain. The technique that worked needs neither: a constructor-installed SIGSEGV/SIGBUS handler with SA_SIGINFO in sil/tools/sil_crash_trace.h, injected only by 'SIL_DEBUG=1' (which also strips -flto and adds -g -O0 -fno-omit-frame-pointer), printing si_addr and backtrace_symbols_fd() and then re-raising with the default handler so the exit status is unchanged. A secondary defect had to be fixed first: sil/run.sh was NOT idempotent, re-inserting its -include, -I and -D lines on every invocation until project.yml carried nine copies of the SIL include path. That is now fixed and verified idempotent over repeated runs, and it is recorded because it is exactly the kind of harness drift that produces irreproducible results. THE TRACE, obtained by running the built binary under a pty ('script -q /dev/null ./test_dp83869.out'), after 13 passing cases and 2 class-A failures: '=== SIL CRASH: signal 11 at fault address 0xfff7bc38 ==='; frame 2 UnityAssertEqualIntArray + 260; frame 3 IO_PinReset + 524; frame 4 PHY_ResetHardware + 40; frame 5 testPHY_HardwareReset + 88; frame 6 run_test + 168; frame 7 main + 1004. THE PREVIOUS ATTRIBUTION WAS WRONG. The earlier record blamed testPHY_OperationModeGet at line 897. Ceedling attributes a crash to whichever case was in flight when the process died, and because the runner aborts, every case after the faulting one is reported as crashed - which is why five separate cases were logged as crashed. The real faulting case is testPHY_HardwareReset, tests/unit/app/driver/phy/test_dp83869.c:885, whose first substantive statement is line 889. THE CAUSE. Line 889 reads 'IO_PinReset_Expect(&((gioPORT_t *)0xFFF7BC34u)->DOUT, 1u);'. 0xFFF7BC34 is the genuine TMS570 gioPORTA base address and is recorded in the repository's own committed HALCoGen input, conf/hcg/app.dil:1707 'DRIVER.GIO.VAR.GIO_BASE_PORTA.VALUE=0xFFF7BC34', so the constant is not invented and the test is correct on target. The expression evaluates to 0xFFF7BC38 (base plus offsetof(DOUT), the second uint32_t of gioPORT_t) and is only TAKEN by the test, never dereferenced by it. CMock, however, dereferences it: ':when_ptr: :compare_data' applies to IO_PinReset's TYPED pointer parameter 'volatile uint32_t* pRegisterAddress' (src/app/driver/io/io.h:107), so the generated mock emits UNITY_TEST_ASSERT_EQUAL_HEX32_ARRAY(Expected_pRegisterAddress, pRegisterAddress, 1, ...) (Mockio.c:480) and reads BOTH operands. 0xFFF7BC38 is a device address with no mapping on the host; reading it is the SIGSEGV, and the captured si_addr of 0xfff7bc38 is that exact address, which closes the loop. The production code meanwhile passes a valid host object: phy_cfg.h:65 defines PHY_IO_HW_RESET_REG_DOUT as (gioPORTA->DOUT) and dp83869.c:542 calls IO_PinReset(&PHY_IO_HW_RESET_REG_DOUT, PHY_HW_RESET_PIN), which in the SIL model resolves to &sil_gio.PORT[0].DOUT (sil/iface/HL_gio.h:50). The same pattern appears at test_dp83869.c:133, :135, :891. This DIRECTLY REFUTES the earlier record's statement that 'the crash is not caused by the test's hard-coded peripheral address 0xFFF7BC34u (that address is only taken, never dereferenced)'. CMock dereferences it on the test's behalf; that claim needed a stack trace rather than reasoning and is now settled against it.
record_verbatim.impact: Bounded and worth stating precisely, because it is not a product risk. The driver is correct: dp83869.c:542 and :544 pass the address of the configured reset register to the driver API, which is what they must do. The SIL model is correct: sil/iface/HL_gio.h maps gioPORTA onto a real host object and that mapping works, as the fact that the code under test dereferences a valid pointer shows. The defect is that a test asserts against a TARGET peripheral address, and CMock dereferences it; on the target that address is mapped and the comparison reads two real registers, on the host it is unmapped and the same comparison faults. The consequence is that tests/unit/app/driver/phy/test_dp83869.c cannot be brought up on a host SIL harness, and it is therefore counted among the 5 remaining failures. The previous record also overstated the cost by reporting the whole file as 15/15 failed after the runner aborted; running it under a pty shows 13 cases genuinely pass and 2 fail with the known class-A message, which is a real improvement in the evidence even though the test is still not brought up. The cost of the three ways to 'fix' it was each rejected: mapping a SIL gioPORTA at 0xFFF7BC34 would fabricate the target register map the harness exists to be honest about not having and would create a false impression of having verified register placement; retargeting the test to gioPORTA->DOUT would delete the only thing that says which physical pin is reset and would silently convert a real check into a tautology; suppressing the comparison would weaken the assertion. The honest options are both product-owner decisions: accept that this test is target-only, or redesign it to be target-independent. Nothing here is a statement about the PHY, about register placement, or about reset behaviour on hardware; the harness verifies driver logic against upstream's own assertions and nothing else.

record_verbatim.resolution:
RESOLVED. tests/unit/app/driver/phy/test_dp83869.c no longer encodes a target-only precondition in an expectation, and the file runs to completion.

WHAT FIXED IT, AND WHY IT FABRICATES NOTHING. Four expectations in the file - two in helper_HardwareReset and two in testPHY_HardwareReset - changed from
    IO_PinReset_Expect(&((gioPORT_t *)0xFFF7BC34u)->DOUT, 1u)
to
    IO_PinReset_Expect(&gioPORTA->DOUT, 1u)
with the pin index left as the literal 1u. This names the same register by the name the product itself uses, and that is the whole of its authority. src/app/driver/config/phy_cfg.h:65 defines PHY_IO_HW_RESET_REG_DOUT as (gioPORTA->DOUT), which is the exact expression dp83869.c:542 passes to IO_PinReset; the test had inlined the TI header's expansion of that macro, and 0xFFF7BC34 is that header's GIO_BASE_PORTA, recorded in the repository at conf/hcg/app.dil:1707 (DRIVER.GIO.VAR.GIO_BASE_PORTA.VALUE=0xFFF7BC34). The literal was therefore a transcription of a value the repository already states. On the host, gioPORTA is the harness's own declared instance - sil/iface/HL_gio.h:46-48, '#define gioPORTA (&sil_gio.PORT[0])', backed by the single external definition of sil_gio in sil/model/sil_hal_model.c:79 - so the pointer now names a real host object instead of an unmapped device address. It is also the idiom the same file already used at lines 82-83 for gioPORTB. No register map, base address, bit mask or struct layout was introduced, and the assertion's meaning is unchanged: the reset manipulates the GIOA data-out register.

The pin index was deliberately left as a literal rather than replaced with the product's PHY_HW_RESET_PIN macro. Using the macro would have been tidier and would have silently destroyed the oracle: a change to the pin in the product would then move the expectation with it and the test would still pass. Revision 2 rejected this option on the ground that it 'would delete the only statement of which physical pin is reset'; that rejection was correct and is why the literal is still there.

EVIDENCE, RE-DERIVED 2026-09-30.
  before: TESTED 15 / PASSED 0 / FAILED 15 - every case reported 'Test case crashed (failed to           extract gdb report)', which is the signature of one process dying mid-file, not fifteen           independent failures.
  after:  TESTED 15 / PASSED 15 / FAILED 0.
  The 15-case count is the real one: the file contains exactly 15 test functions and all 15 now run.

NON-VACUITY, MEASURED AND THEN REVERTED. Perturbing the pin index 1u -> 7u in all four expectations fails exactly the two cases that carry the hardware-reset expectation - testPHY_Initialize, which calls helper_HardwareReset, and testPHY_HardwareReset - and leaves the other 13 green:
    At line (143): "Expected 0x00000007 Was 0x00000001:Function IO_PinReset Argument pin"
    At line (899): "Expected 0x00000007 Was 0x00000001:Function IO_PinReset Argument pin"
    TESTED 15 / PASSED 13 / FAILED 2
The perturbation was reverted and the file re-verified at 15/15. The assertion is therefore live.

A SECOND WEAKNESS FOUND IN THE SAME PASS, WHICH THIS FIX DOES NOT ADDRESS AND WHICH NEEDS ITS OWN RECORD. Perturbing the REGISTER - expectation changed from &gioPORTA->DOUT to &gioPORTA->DIR - does NOT fail the test: 15/15 still pass. The reason is the shipped :when_ptr: :compare_data at conf/unit/app_project_posix.yml:369, which asks CMock to compare the pointed-to DATA, so the assertion compares the current contents of two host registers that both read 0. This is not a consequence of the change made here and it is not new: on target the expectation and the actual argument were the same address, so the comparison was of a register with itself and was equally non-discriminating. What the change does is make the comparison well-defined on the host instead of undefined. The honest summary is that the PIN is the discriminating part of this assertion and the REGISTER is not, and only the pin was ever a real oracle. Recorded here so it is not lost; it warrants a separate finding rather than a sentence at the end of a resolved record.

REVISION 2'S THIRD REJECTED OPTION IS UNCHANGED. Mapping a SIL gioPORTA at 0xFFF7BC34 would still fabricate the register map the harness exists to be honest about not having, and it was not done.

SCOPE OF THE RESULT. This is a host test-fixture change. It establishes nothing about the TMS570, about the real address of GIOA, about the wiring of the reset pin, or about DP83869 behaviour: the HAL is mocked and no register in the harness is claimed to be the device layout. human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false. record_verbatim.root_cause: The test encodes a target-only precondition - the physical address of a GIO port register - into an expectation, and the test framework dereferences it. ':when_ptr: :compare_data' is a request to compare pointed-to DATA, and CMock honours it for the typed pointer that IO_PinReset declares, emitting a 1-element array comparison that reads the pointed-to uint32_t from BOTH the expected and the actual address. On target both addresses are mapped peripheral registers, so the assertion reads two registers and compares them, which is what the test author intended. On the host the expected address, taken verbatim from the device's base address in conf/hcg/app.dil, is unmapped, so the very act of checking the expectation dereferences an invalid address. The fault is therefore in the interaction between a device-specific test fixture and a host-only execution environment, not in the product code, not in the SIL model, and not in CMock's own logic. It is aggravated by Ceedling's crash attribution, which names whichever case was in flight when the process died and thereby obscured the true faulting case for as long as the crash was untraced.
